source.title: Scaling Laws for Fact Memorization of Large Language Models
source.authors: Xing-Yu Lu; Xiaonan Li; Qinyuan Cheng; Kai Ding; Xuan-Jing Huang; Xi-Peng Qiu

page_placements.theme: Memorization and factual binding depend on capacity, exposure and architecture

record.tranche_reason: Tests loss scaling in a structured atomic-fact training and generalization setting, rather than ordinary language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a power-law fit for held-out fact-generalization loss as training fact quantity varies. Its fact-capacity scaling results are also recorded, but capacity is not loss and therefore does not test the named loss versions. Cited results about general pretraining and downstream scaling are not this study's results. Other fact-memorization experiments on redundancy, frequency, difficulty, and order do not measure the claim's scaling outcomes.
record.test_reason: Section 6 fits a power law to held-out test loss against training-set size, for LMs trained from scratch on structured fact triples over many epochs. That is a new training regime for the loss–data power law (V5). The setting is not ordinary text pretraining, so V1 itself is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that fact capacity is linear in model size and follows a negative exponential in epochs, so memorizing all of Wikidata would need about 1000B non-embedding parameters at 100 epochs. They also conclude that fact-generalization test loss follows a power law in training-fact count, similar to Kaplan et al.
record.recipe_differences: Uses structured (key, attribute, value) fact prediction, measures exact-match memorization and test loss on unseen facts, and varies fact quantity, parameter count, or epochs; it does not reproduce the original general-language pretraining loss or compute-allocation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that learning rates are sensitive to model size and dataset and selects different rates; Figure 11 reports fact-generalization loss for two model sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Fact capacity scales linearly with non-embedding parameters (company table at 50 and 200 epochs; Wikidata at 100 epochs). A fit on small models extrapolates to the 308M non-embedding model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Exact-match fact-memorization capacity scales linearly with non-embedding parameter count, and small-model fits extrapolate about 8x.

fits_no_version.finding: Fact capacity rises with training epochs and saturates near 1000 epochs, following a negative exponential fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fact-memorization capacity against training epochs follows a saturating negative exponential.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The authors state that the experiments use a maximum model size of 0.5B because of computational limits. The main fact-generalization loss curves are shown in figures without numerical values or reported uncertainty. The paper notes that its atomic-fact setup, with the same inputs for training and inference, differs from ordinary pretraining on unstructured text.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded the paper's separate results on redundant facts, abstract-ability learning, fact frequency/difficulty/order, and fact generalization accuracy because they do not measure the scaling-loss claim versions. Excluded cited results from other studies.

untested.parts: Image, video and other modalities; fine-tuning and transfer. Only structured fact-triple training with test loss against data size is tested; parameter and compute scaling of loss are not tested.
Held-out loss on ordinary text pretraining against parameters, tokens or compute.
No loss extrapolation; only capacity extrapolation.
No variation of model shape at fixed parameter count.
No analysis of how fits depend on setup or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The V5 support is weak: the power law covers only about one decade of data size, has no reported exponent, and comes from two small models. The epochs used for the Fig. 11 runs are unstated, and the regime is multi-epoch repeated training on triples. Capacity results are excluded from all versions because they do not measure loss.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
It extrapolates fact capacity, not held-out loss of larger runs.
No fixed-compute budget or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is measured.
Architecture details are not varied at fixed parameter count to measure their effect on loss.
Tests structured fact generalization, not image/video modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer.
The paper does not test downstream task performance scaling; its fact generalization evaluation is not a downstream-task study.
It does not investigate how scaling-law fits or compute-optimal allocations change with setup or fitting choices.
